value: The premier Filipino-Chinese student-led organization of the Ateneo de Manila University.
3/F Manuel V. Pangilinan Building, Ateneo de Manila University, Katipunan Avenue, Quezon City
Six departments, one community. Celadon runs the projects, culture, and formation that carry Filipino-Chinese life on campus — and recruits the students who make them happen.

Established in 1985, Ateneo Celadon is the premier Chinese-Filipino organization of the Ateneo for 40 years running. We aspire to develop our members to become the game changers in society by integrating our vision of social change with the Chinese-Filipino tradition. In Celadon, we encourage our members to be united in this vision by developing their potential to become globally competitive leaders based on strong Chinese-Filipino principles. We do this by showcasing our events such as cultural festivals, financial summits, and leadership programs that not only have won awards but also bring the best in our members–paving the way for them to become the leaders and visionaries for a 'Greater Philippine Society'. With the help our partners such as the Ateneo Ricardo Leong Center for Chinese Studies, we believe this is possible. Simply put, Celadon has stayed and will stay true to its promise of being the forefront in creating Chinese-Filipino game-changers for the country.

Every project on this site was run by students. Each one is staffed by a core team drawn from across the organization, supported by six departments that handle communications, culture, external relations, finance, people, and strategy.
Ateneo Celadon envisions a community that is deeply connected to Chinese-Filipino culture and is committed to engaging in its identity, appreciation, and discourse within greater Philippine society.

Ateneo Celadon strives to engage its members and audiences in learning, experiencing, and facilitating exchange between the Chinese-Filipino culture and greater Philippine society through culturally-rooted efforts. In line with this, the organization aims to develop member relations and equip them with different skills that are relevant to the practice and discourse of Chinese-Filipino culture.

Chinese-Filipino values are rooted in openness, sensitivity, excellence, and family.
